items.name: Readability
items.evidence: There are no comments on the `#if 0` / `r""" "` language switch or on the base-1e9 bignum loop (`cap = (int)(n / 40) + 4`, `% 1000000000ULL`). The business logic uses single-letter names `a`, `b`, `n` and terse names `cap`, `len`, which caps this item at accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: All the C logic (parsing, bignum Fibonacci, printing) sits in one `main` with no helper function. Python has the `hasattr(sys, "set_int_max_str_digits")` guard, which is dead code on the stated 3.12. The file is small and has no duplicated paths.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: C uses `atol` with no validation, so non-numeric input prints 0. `calloc` results are never checked for NULL. The constants `40`, `4` and `1000000000ULL` are unnamed. Python has no argv check, so a missing argument raises an IndexError traceback. Memory is freed and nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: f(0), f(1) and large n are correct and iterative in both languages, with bignum agreement verified up to n=500. Argument errors are mostly not handled: C `if (argc < 2) return 1;` gives no message, and negative or non-numeric input prints `0` with exit 0. Python crashes with a traceback rather than printing a usage message.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: Works with exactly the two given commands and no extra flags. It compiled cleanly even under -Wall -Wextra -pedantic, and the `#if 0` lines contain balanced quotes. Both modes print only the number, and outputs matched for n=0..500.
